QuestionStmt.S: Which of the following equations is correct regarding rate of disappearance of reactant and appearance of product for $$\mathrm{N_2(g) + 3H_2(g) \rightarrow 2NH_3(g)}$$

Solution.S:
For the reaction $\mathrm{N_2 + 3H_2 \rightarrow 2NH_3}$, the rate of reaction can be expressed as:

$$\text{Rate} = -\frac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = -\frac{1}{3} \frac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt} = \frac{1}{2} \frac{d[\mathrm{NH_3}]}{dt}$$

Rearranging: $\frac{1}{2} \frac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = \frac{1}{3} \frac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt}$ (with proper sign consideration). This matches option B.
